To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
large cells are more active in lipogenesis than small cells in a heterogeneous sample of sheep adipose tissue.
adipose cell size is inversely related to adipose cell lipogenesis.

large adipose (fat) cells are much more active than small adipose cells in synthesizing fatty acids from glucose and that large adipose cell size is associated with high rates of fatty acid synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the study of the relationship between adipocyte size and lipogenesis.
the study of the relationship between adipocyte cell size and lipogenetic activity in a heterogeneous population.

the relationship between the size and lipogenic capacity of adipose cells and the role of the adipose cell in the regulation of the metabolism of glucose and lipids in adipose tissue and the whole animal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the large cells are more active than the small cells in the synthesis of lipids.
the adipose cell is a heterogeneous population of individual cells with respect to size, lipogenic activity, and lipid content.
adipose tissue is not composed of a single cell type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the larger cells of a given adipose tissue are more active in the formation of lipid than the smaller cells.
the size and the activity of individual adipose cells are closely related.
large adipose cell size is associated with increased rates of lipogenesis and decreased rates of lipolysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adipose cell size is a major determinant of lipogenic activity in adipose tissue.
adipose tissue is a heterogeneous tissue and the adipocytes that make up this tissue are not all equal.
the size of the adipose cell is a major determinant of its lipogenic capacity.
